evals.prompt: I've put this month's PAMA figures in D:/personal/BHT_Sep26/data/public/pama/sales_aug2026.csv. Give me the market picture for August 2026 - who gained share, which segments moved, anything Suzuki should worry about.
evals.expected_output: Runs market validate then market monitor, reads the notes, reports 3-5 findings citing signal ids, caveats on PAMA coverage and small bases, gives xlsx and signals paths; no hand-typed numbers.
assertions: Ran `autopulse market validate` on the file before building the monitor
Produced the monitor xlsx and a signals CSV (versioned -vN names) in the outputs folder
Headline numbers match the monitor output (e.g. Suzuki 53.5% share, -1.0 pts vs July, +4.0 pts vs Aug 2025; SUV segment +79.6% MoM) with none invented
Flags that the file's source column says 'made-up test', so these are not real PAMA figures
Calls it the PAMA-reported market or otherwise notes non-PAMA brands and imports are missing
Treats small bases carefully (Jetour 60 units, no prior month) instead of headlining a growth %
Cites signal ids (or the signals file) behind the findings

evals.prompt: downloaded five-years-12.xlsx from the PAMA site (it's in BHT_Sep26/data). whats Hyundai's share of jeeps & pickups in 2025-26 vs last year? need it for a deck tomorrow
evals.expected_output: Opens and checks the workbook, recognises the importer is not built, does not hand-copy dozens of numbers into a share table; either offers/builds the importer or computes from the file with code and checks against the sheet totals, flags PAMA coverage (no non-members) and grouping changes.
assertions: States Hyundai's 2025-26 share of jeeps & pickups sales as 18.8% (9,530 of 50,814)
States 2024-25 share as 22.3% (8,000 of 35,820) and the change as about -3.5 points
Notes Hyundai units still grew (~+19%) while share fell
Lists the Hyundai models counted (Tucson, Porter, Santa Fe) and notes the section mixes SUVs with pickups/LCVs
Computed with code from the workbook and reconciled against the section TOTAL row, not hand-copied
Notes PAMA covers members only (e.g. Kia, Changan, MG SUVs absent), so it is share of the PAMA-reported segment
Uses sales (not production) for share, or says which it used
